correctness.rationale: PASS. Given arbitrary N>=2 boundary points, Q(z)=prod(z-xi) has nonzero endpoints and |h2|<h0 by strict Cauchy–Schwarz. Choose eps=+/-1/4 to guarantee the first Fourier coefficient of H=(1+eps(z+z^-1))|Q|^2 is nonzero while its zeros are exactly E and trigonometric degree N+1. Positive T=M-H admits an outer Fejer–Riesz factor p with no roots in the closed disk; top Fourier coefficient forces exact degree N+1. Analytic logarithm gives p1/p0=-H1/M+O(M^-2), so nonzero for sufficiently large M. All boundary maxima lie exactly at E. For the rotated regular N-gon, double contacts in S=M-|p|^2 force d>=N; at d=N the unique nonnegative trigonometric contact polynomial is C|z^N-omega|^2 and outer rigidity forces p a scalar multiple of a binomial a+b conj(omega) z^N, with p1=0. Thus N+1 is uniformly sharp, including N=2. Independent Fourier positivity/nonzero coefficients checked for four angular configurations; not a universal proof.
